note: Hand-written, and deliberately not produced by the generator: vectors it
produced would only prove that it agrees with itself (ADR-0013).
Values are hex so that a reader can check a value against its bytes by eye —
0x01020304 little-endian is 04 03 02 01. Both languages read this file,
encode the values and compare bytes, then decode the bytes and compare values.
A command's zero bytes are a promise: a slot is reused, and a writer fills
the whole payload rather than only the fields it declares. The tests start
from a slot full of 0xaa so that the promise is what is being tested.
A buffer of samples has no byte vector: 8 KB of hex would prove nothing that
a plane offset does not. It has an entry under arrays instead, because in
Rust a plane offset is a static assertion rustc checks, while in TypeScript
it is arithmetic inside a generated function that nothing else checks.
Offsets, lengths and enum codes are written in decimal: they are numbers to
compare, not bytes to read off.
No value here reads the same backwards. 0x00000000 and 0xffffffff would let
